title: European search engine Ecosia drops Mistral and eyes Chinese AI models
source_used: PPC Land and Trending Topics, both relaying POLITICO Europe (Cybernews and POLITICO blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: POLITICO Europe published an interview with Ecosia chief executive Christian Kroll on 6 Oct 2026.
Ecosia, a Berlin search engine, is replacing Mistral as its AI model supplier; it had switched from OpenAI to Mistral only in May.
Kroll called Mistral's models 'a year behind', said servers were overloaded ('We were simply too large a customer') and said reliance on international investors was 'not truly sovereign'.
Ecosia now uses open-weight models, including China's Qwen, GLM and Kimi, hosted by the German platform Melious.
Kroll says costs roughly halved while quality and performance improved; POLITICO prints no baseline for that figure.
Mistral did not respond to POLITICO's request for comment; chief scientist Guillaume Lample said on 5 Oct that Mistral's new model should be tested.
Mistral released Large 4 on 6 Oct, a 1-trillion-parameter model with weights due by the end of October.
quote_evidence: Kroll described the French company's models as "a year behind" the competition.
"We've roughly cut our costs in half while improving quality and performance," Kroll said.
Mistral did not respond to POLITICO's request for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: Europe's best-known AI company loses a visible customer to open and Chinese models.
notes: Original reporter is POLITICO Europe (interview of 6 Oct); Cybernews (pool source) blocked. Read PPC Land and Trending Topics relaying POLITICO; POLITICO's own page returned 403, link decoded from Google News. Event predates the 8 Oct window start.
